name: Gershom
title: Moses' firstborn son
summary: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah. His name means "a stranger there," and was given because Moses said: "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land." Gershom belonged to the tribe of Levi, and his descendants served as priests and Levites in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Gershom in Midian
keyEvents.description: Moses had his firstborn son with Zipporah in Midian and named him Gershom, because he was a foreigner in a foreign land.

keyEvents.title: Zipporah Circumcises Her Son
keyEvents.description: On the way back to Egypt, the Lord confronted Moses, and Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint stone to save Moses' life.

keyEvents.title: Jethro brings the family back to Moses
keyEvents.description: After the exodus from Egypt, Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, back to Moses in the wilderness at the mountain of God.

keyEvents.title: The descendants of Gershom among the Levites
keyEvents.description: Gershom's sons were counted among the tribe of Levi and given duties related to the tabernacle and the temple.

keyEvents.title: Gershom's descendants as priests in Dan
keyEvents.description: Jonathan, son of Gershom, Moses' son, and his sons served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the people were taken into exile from the land.

keyEvents.title: The lineage of Gershom in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In David's time, Gershom's descendants were registered and assigned tasks in temple service. Shebuel, one of Gershom's descendants, was placed over the treasuries.
